units.text: Electric current's SI base unit is the ampere, not the kelvin, as the 2019 SI defines kelvin as the base unit for thermodynamic temperature. Multiple sources confirm ampere is the base unit for electric current.

citations.title: The International System of Units (SI), 2019 Edition

judgement.reason: NIST and BIPM passages confirm the ampere is the SI unit for electric current, but none of the passages states that the kelvin is the base unit for thermodynamic temperature, so that factual part is unsupported.
